newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to discuss Vale's sale early Sept.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to discuss Vale's sale early Sept.

text.p: Brazil's National Privatization Council (CND) will meet early in September to discuss the model for the sale of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), said Jose Pio Borges, vice-president of the National Development Bank (BNDES).

The CND was previously scheduled to meet on August 29, but the meeting was postponed because Planning Minister Antonio Kandir, who heads the council, is involved in talks for the approval of a bill to exempt exporters from the so-called ICMS tax on sales and services.

The model for Vale's privatization, which is being designed by a group of advisors led by Merrill Lynch, is almost completed and is expected to call for the creation of a holding company by the new majority shareholders.

According to a draft proposal, the government would auction 45 percent of its 76 percent stake in the company's voting capital under a block sale. The group of investors that acquire the 45 percent stake in Vale would commit itself to create the holding.
The holding would replace the shareholders agreement that normally follows privatizations when shares are sold to a group of investors.
With the approval of Vale's privatization model, tender documents will be published late September or early October, said Pio Borges, who is also BNDES's Privatization chief.
Vale is expected to be privatized in February 1997.
